title: Countable simplicial intervals detect equivalence lifting
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, boundaries and horns [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A small simplicial category has a set of objects, simplicial mapping sets, identity vertices and associative unital simplicial composition. Let $\mathrm{sCat}$ be their category, with arbitrary object functions on enriched functors. It is complete, cocomplete and locally presentable: for some regular cardinal $\kappa$ it is generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. For a fixed object set $O$, the category $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ of simplicial categories and functors equal to the identity on $O$ has a cofibrantly generated model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations; its cofibrations are retracts of free simplicial extensions (degreewise free enriched-category extensions with degeneracies preserving the chosen free generators).

For a simplicial set $K$, let $U(K)$ have objects $0,1$, mapping set $K$ from $0$ to $1$, identity mapping sets $\Delta^0$, and empty mapping set from $1$ to $0$. Let $I$ consist of $\varnothing\to\{0\}$ and $U(\partial\Delta^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ for $n\geq0$. Let $J$ consist of $U(\Lambda_i^n)\to U(\Delta^n)$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$, and $\{0\}\to H$ for a set of representatives of two-object simplicial categories $H$ with all four mapping sets weakly contractible, countably many simplices in each mapping set, and $\{0\}\amalg\{1\}\to H$ a cofibration in $\mathrm{sCat}_{\{0,1\}}$. Write $K\text{-inj}$ for maps with the right lifting property against $K$, $K\text{-cof}$ for maps with the left lifting property against $K\text{-inj}$, and $K\text{-cell}$ for transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of maps in $K$. Both $I$ and $J$ admit functorial small-object factorizations as a $K\text{-cell}$ map followed by a $K\text{-inj}$ map; every $K\text{-cof}$ map is a retract of a $K\text{-cell}$ map. Every map of $J$ belongs to $I\text{-cof}$.

For a simplicial functor $p:A\to B$, membership in $J\text{-inj}$ is equivalent to the conjunction of: each $A(a,a')\to B(pa,pa')$ is a Kan fibration; and for every object $a$ of $A$ and every vertex $e:pa\to b$ invertible in $\pi_0 B$, there are an object $a'$ with $pa'=b$ and a vertex $d:a\to a'$ invertible in $\pi_0 A$ with $p(d)=e$ as vertices. Here $\pi_0$ takes components of each mapping set, and invertible means having a two-sided inverse in this ordinary category.

source.place: Section 1, generating sets (C1),(C2),(A1),(A2); Section 2, Propositions 2.3 and 2.5 and Lemma 2.4; Section 3, smallness and small-object factorizations. Local presentability: HTT Appendix A.3.2 (categories enriched in the locally presentable cartesian category of simplicial sets). No Stacks tag states this enriched interval result.

proof.text: Present strict simplicial categories by the following finite-limit sketch. There is a sort $O$ of objects and, for every $n\geq0$, a sort $M_n$ of arrows in degree $n$, source and target maps $M_n\rightrightarrows O$, identities $O\to M_n$, all simplicial operators $M_n\to M_m$, and composition on the specified pullback of pairs with matching middle object. Impose the category laws in each degree, the simplicial identities, and preservation of source, target, identities and composition by each simplicial operator; the operators on $O$ are the identity. These are exactly the data and laws of the stated simplicial categories, and maps of models are exactly enriched functors with arbitrary object functions. The sketch is small and every specified cone is finite. Apply [lem-coef-finite-limit-model-presentability]: its models are complete, cocomplete and locally finitely presentable, in particular locally presentable as required. It also gives filtered colimits on these displayed sorts, used in step 4.

source.place: Sections 4 and 9, especially (9.3), (9.7), (9.8); explicit sketch supplied here

proof.text: For a fixed small set $O$, use the algebraic theory with sorts $(a,b)\in O^2$, binary operations $M(b,c)\times M(a,b)\to M(a,c)$ and identity constants in $M(a,a)$, subject to associativity and the unit equations. These operations are total on each specified pair of sorts; empty off-diagonal sorts are permitted. Its strict simplicial algebras are precisely $\mathrm{sCat}_O$. The free functor for the sort $(a,b)$ freely adjoins arrows from $a$ to $b$ labelled by a simplicial set, including free words when $a=b$. [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model] therefore gives the objectwise Kan model structure and generating boundary/horn cells, including cells at equal endpoints.

Describe these boundary cells explicitly to obtain the claimed free-map characterization. A pushout of a free boundary inclusion adjoins an $n$-simplex generator with its faces already prescribed, together with its degeneracies and all composable words. In degree $k$ the new free generators are exactly the degeneracies in degree $k$ of the attached simplex not already in the boundary. The only reductions of words compose adjacent old arrows or remove identities; reduced words alternating old arrows and new generators give the free-product normal form. Iterating the attachments preserves this normal form and makes degeneracies carry free generators to free generators. Conversely, for a degreewise free extension with degeneracy-stable chosen generators, attach its generators not obtained by degeneracy in increasing degree. Their faces have lower degree, so are already attached; this realizes the extension by free boundary cells. Cofibrations are retracts of these cell maps by [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model], and the converse follows because each free extension is such a cell map and cofibrations are retract closed. Thus cofibrations are precisely retracts of the stated free extensions.

source.place: Section 2, Definitions 2.1–2.2 and the following free-map characterization; normal-form explanation supplied here

proof.text: Both generating families are sets. In particular a countable two-object interval can be relabelled so that every degree of every mapping set is a subset of $\mathbb N$; all simplicial operators and composition functions then belong to a set of coded structures. Choosing representatives preserves the labelled objects and the distinguished inclusion of object 0. All the domains in $I$ and $J$ are $\varnothing$, $\{0\}$, or $U(K)$ for a boundary or a horn with finitely many nondegenerate simplices. A functor from $U(K)$ is just two object choices and a simplicial map from $K$ into their mapping set. It is specified by finitely many object/arrow elements and finitely many face equalities. Since filtered colimits on the sketch sorts are computed in sets by [lem-coef-finite-limit-model-presentability], all these elements and equalities occur at a common stage; equality of two such functors also occurs at a common stage. The same argument with no arrows handles $\{0\}$, and the empty domain is immediate. Thus Hom from every generating domain preserves filtered colimits, hence the continuous countable chains in [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization]. Apply that node with $\kappa=\aleph_0$ separately to $I$ and $J$, using cocompleteness from step 1. It gives the required functorial cell/injective factorizations and exactly the stated retract characterization of $K$-cof.

source.place: Section 1, (A2), and proof of Theorem 1.1 at the end of Section 3; smallness checked explicitly via the sketch

proof.text: A square against $U(K)\to U(L)$, whose object map is the identity on the two labels, is exactly a square $K\to A(a,a')$, $L\to B(pa,pa')$ with fixed endpoints, even if $a=a'$. The free meaning of $U$ follows directly since it has no composable nonidentity arrows. The empty-to-singleton generator tests surjectivity on objects. The boundary characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore says that $I$-inj consists exactly of the object-surjective functors with mappingwise trivial Kan fibrations. Given such a functor and any $J$-generator, lift its second target object by object-surjectivity if it is an interval generator, and retain the two already specified objects if it is a horn generator. For these labelled choices form $A_O(i,j)=A(a_i,a_j)$ and $B_O(i,j)=B(pa_i,pa_j)$, using two labels whether or not their images coincide. The induced functor in $\mathrm{sCat}_{\{0,1\}}$ is a trivial fibration by [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. For an interval the discrete-two-object map into $H$ is a cofibration by its defining condition; for a horn use its generating trivial cofibration in the same sorted model structure. The corresponding fixed-object lift gives the original lift. Thus every $J$-generator has the left lifting property against every member of $I$-inj, which is exactly $J\subset I$-cof.

source.place: Section 1, generating sets; Section 2 fixed-object lifting; Section 3, Proposition 3.2

proof.text: By the same explicit square correspondence, the horn part of $J$ tests exactly the local Kan fibration condition, using [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Suppose now that $p$ lies in $J$-inj, and fix an object $a$ and an equivalence vertex $e:pa\to b$ in $B$. Make a two-labelled category $D$ with $D(i,j)=B(b_i,b_j)$ for $b_0=pa$, $b_1=b$, and composition from $B$. It has two distinct labels even if $pa=b$. Apply [lem-coef-countable-equivalence-witness] to the prescribed arrow $e$ to get $F\to H\to D$. After replacing $H$ by its chosen labelled representative, its object-0 inclusion is a generator of $J$. Its lifting square has top object $a$ and bottom $H\to D\to B$, so it admits a functor $H\to A$ over $B$. The image of the specified vertex from $F$ is a vertex $d$ satisfying $p(d)=e$ exactly and with target mapping exactly to $b$. Each mapping set of $H$ is nonempty and connected, so $\pi_0H$ has exactly one arrow between every two objects. Hence that specified vertex is invertible and its image $d$ is invertible in $\pi_0A$. This proves the required strict vertex-lifting condition, including repeated endpoints.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, using Lemma 2.4; duplicate-labelled endpoint construction on printed p. 6

proof.text: Conversely assume the local Kan condition and the strict equivalence-vertex lifting condition. Horn squares lift by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For an interval square with top object $a_0$ and bottom $v:H\to B$, choose a vertex $g\in H(0,1)_0$. Its component is invertible since all four mapping sets are weakly contractible. The vertex $v(g)$ lifts, by the assumed equivalence-vertex condition, to an invertible $d:a_0\to a_1$ with $pa_1=v(1)$ and $p(d)=v(g)$. Define two-labelled categories $A_O(i,j)=A(a_i,a_j)$ and $B_O(i,j)=B(v(i),v(j))$. The induced $p_O:A_O\to B_O$ is a local Kan fibration; the construction permits $a_0=a_1$ and permits $v(0)=v(1)$. Form the strict fixed-object pullback $E=A_O\times_{B_O}H$. Its projection $t:E\to H$ is mappingwise a Kan fibration: a horn square projects to one for $p_O$ and its filler, paired with the given simplex in $H$, is the required pullback filler. The compatible vertex $(d,g)$ has both projections invertible, so [lem-coef-simplicial-pullback-equivalence] makes it invertible in $\pi_0E$. Apply [lem-coef-countable-equivalence-witness] to it. This gives an interval $H'$ and an object-preserving functor $z:H'\to E$. The composite $w=tz:H'\to H$ is a mappingwise weak equivalence, since each of its source and target mapping sets is weakly contractible. Notice that it need not preserve a chosen arrow as a cofibration; only the discrete two-object inclusion into $H$ will be used next.

source.place: Proposition 2.5, pullback construction on printed pp. 7–8; explicit compatibility check and labelled categories supplied here

proof.text: Work in the fixed-object model structure of [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. Factor the weak equivalence $w:H'\to H$ as a trivial cofibration $j:H'\to T$ followed by a fibration $r:T\to H$. Two-out-of-three makes $r$ a trivial fibration. Since $t:E\to H$ is a fibration, the square with top $z:H'\to E$, bottom $r:T\to H$ and left $j$ has a filler $h:T\to E$ with $th=r$. Since $O\to H$ is a cofibration and $r$ a trivial fibration, the square $O\to T$, $H\xrightarrow{1}H$ has a filler $s:H\to T$ with $rs=1_H$. Thus $hs:H\to E$ is a section of $t$. Composing with $E\to A_O\to A$ gives a functor over the original $v:H\to B$, sending object 0 to the originally prescribed $a_0$. A map out of the singleton category contains only this object and its identities, so this is exactly a filler of the original interval square. All interval and horn generators therefore lift, proving $p\in J$-inj. Together with step 6 this proves the equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.5 and Lemma 2.6; use the cofibration O→H instead of an unassumed cofibration F→H

Sources read online: Bergner math/0406507 §1 (C1),(C2),(A1),(A2),(F1),(F2), Prop 2.3, Lemma 2.4 with §4 (Lemmas 4.1–4.3), Prop 2.5, Lemma 2.6; and Bergner math/0508152 Def 3.1, Example 3.5, Def 3.6, Thm 4.7 with proof (printed pp. 1937–1944). Steps: (1) the finite-limit sketch models exactly simplicial categories with arbitrary object maps, so locally finitely presentable with sortwise filtered colimits. (2) The O^2-sorted theory is Example 3.5, with free words when a=b. (3) Free-extension characterization: the normal-form argument is written out and correct; marked elementary, which is generous but accepted. (4) Finite generating domains are omega-small, so the small-object leaf applies at aleph_0; J is a set by coding countable H in N. (5) I-inj is object-surjective plus mappingwise trivial fibration, including n=0; J is contained in I-cof via the two-labelled fixed-object lift. lean.statement: theorem simplicial_interval_lifting : HasLimitsOfSize.{u, u} SCat.{u} ∧ HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} SCat.{u} ∧ IsLocallyPresentable.{u} SCat.{u} ∧ (∀ O : Type u, HasLimitsOfSize.{u, u} (Fixed O) ∧ HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (Fixed O) ∧ ∃ m : ModelCategory (Fixed O), m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences = fixedWeakEquivalences O ∧ m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations = fixedFibrations O ∧ m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations = fixedCofibrations O ∧ IsCofibrantlyGeneratedFixed O ∧ fixedCofibrations O = MorphismProperty.retracts (fun _ _ f ↦ IsFreeExtension (O := O) f)) ∧ SmallObjectConclusions I.{u} ∧ Nonempty IntervalRepresentatives.{u} ∧ ∀ R : IntervalRepresentatives.{u}, SmallObjectConclusions (J R) ∧ J R ≤ I.rlp.llp ∧ ∀ (A B : SCat.{u}) (p : A ⟶ B), (J R).rlp p ↔ IsLocalFibration p ∧ LiftsEquivalenceVertices p
